verses.zh: 「凡有残疾，或有甚么恶病的牛羊，你都不可献给耶和华―你的　神，因为这是耶和华―你　神所憎恶的。
verses.en: You must not sacrifice to him[NOTE:1] a bull or sheep that has a blemish or any other defect, because that is considered offensive[NOTE:2] to the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “to the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 16:1.

The Hebrew word תּוֹעֵבָה (toʿevah, “an abomination”; cf. NAB) describes persons, things, or practices offensive to ritual or moral order. See M. Grisanti, NIDOTTE 4:314-18; see also the note on the word “abhorrent” in Deut 7:25.
verses.commentary:
17:1 "blemish or any defect" This verse is contextually related to Deut. 15:21, which also deals with appropriate
places and types of sacrifices. In the OT "blemish" (BDB 548) refers to any kind of physical defect (cf. Deut. 15:21;
Lev. 22:20-25). Malachi 1:6-8 records an example of Israel giving God less than the best.

verses.en: Suppose a man or woman is discovered among you in one of your villages[NOTE:1] that the Lord your God is giving you who sins before the Lord your God[NOTE:2] and breaks his covenant
notes: Heb “gates.”
Heb “does the evil in the eyes of the Lord your God.”
verses.commentary:
17:2-13 These verses

- deal with administrative justice

- vv. 2-7 deal with idolatry and legal witnesses

- vv. 8-13 deal with the practical setup of the courts

- This is similar to Deut. 16:18-20.

17:2

NASB, NRSV
"who does what is evil"

NKJV
"who has been wicked"

TEV
"has sinned "

NJB, REB
"who does what is wrong"

JPSOA
"who has affronted"

LXX, Peshitta
"who will do what is evil"

This phrase is a Qal IMPERFECT VERB (BDB 793 I, KB 889) and a DIRECT OBJECT
(BDB 948). This is the common two-consonant root ער, which means "bad," "evil," "distress," "misery," "injury," or
"calamity." Here the context defines it as

- "transgressing His covenant," Deut. 17:2 (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
literally "passing over")

- "has gone and served other gods and worshiped them," Deut. 17:3:

- "has gone" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

- "served" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

- "worshiped" ‒ BDB 1005, KB 295, Hishtaphel IMPERFECT with waw

▣ "by transgressing His covenant" This VERB (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) basically means "to pass over" or "pass through." It is most often used in a
literal sense, but sometimes in a theological sense. Originally it may have referred to the act of halving an animal
as a covenant act and walking between the parts (e.g. Gen. 15:17). Violation of the covenant resulted in death or
destruction (i.e. like the halved animal). It denoted the violation of clearly defined actions (i.e. covenant stipulations,
cf. Deut. 26:13; Josh. 7:11,15; Jdg. 2:20; 2 Kgs. 18:12; Jer. 34:18-19; Hosea 6:7; 8:1).

verses.zh: 去事奉敬拜别神，或拜日头，或拜月亮，或拜天象，是主不曾吩咐的；
verses.en: by serving other gods and worshiping them—the sun,[NOTE:1] moon, or any other heavenly bodies that I have not permitted you to worship.[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT reads “and to the sun,” thus including the sun, the moon, and other heavenly spheres among the gods. However, Theodotion and Lucian read “or to the sun,” suggesting perhaps that the sun and the other heavenly bodies are not in the category of actual deities.
Heb “which I have not commanded you.” The words “to worship” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
17:3 "the sun or the moon or any of the heavenly host" The ancient Assyrians and Babylonians may have been the first, but not the
last, to see the heavenly bodies as representatives of gods and goddesses (cf. Deut. 4:19; 2 Kgs. 17:16; 21:3,5; 23:4-5;
2 Chr. 33:3,5; Jer. 8:2; 19:13). They felt that the lights of the sky controlled mankind's destiny (physically and spiritually).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

verses.zh: 有人告诉你，你也听见了，就要细细地探听，果然是真，准有这可憎恶的事行在以色列中，
verses.en: When it is reported to you and you hear about it, you must investigate carefully. If it is indeed true that such a disgraceful thing[NOTE:1] is being done in Israel,
notes: Heb “an abomination” (תּוֹעֵבָה); see note on the word “offensive” in v. 1.
verses.commentary:
17:4 This verse is similar to Deut. 13:14. The VERB "you shall inquire thoroughly" (BDB 205, KB 233,
Qal PERFECT with waw) implies a complete investigation (cf. Deut. 13:14; 17:4,9; 19:18; Lev. 10:16;
Jdgs. 6:29). Accusations and second-hand knowledge were not enough to convict. Israel's judicial system was harsh ("stoned to
death," Deut. 17:5), but thorough.

verses.zh: 你就要将行这恶事的男人或女人拉到城门外，用石头将他打死。
verses.en: you must bring to your city gates[NOTE:1] that man or woman who has done this wicked thing—that very man or woman—and you must stone that person to death.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “gates.”
Heb “stone them with stones so that they die” (KJV similar); NCV “throw stones at that person until he dies.”
verses.commentary:
17:5 "to your gates" This idiomatic phrase meant "to your local court." This was where the local elders sat.

▣ "stone them to death" This was a form of corporate punishment (cf. Deut. 17:7). Every adult member
of the community acted to rid itself of the evil (see full note at Deut. 13:10).

▣ The Hebrew text has a series of VERBS that refer to death in Deut. 17:5-7:

- "stone to death" ‒ BDB 709, KB 768, Qal PERFECT with waw, Deut. 17:5

- death ‒ BDB 559, KB 562

- v. 6, Hophal IMPERFECT

- v. 6, Hophal imPERFECT

- v. 7, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

Covenant violations carried severe consequences (cf. Deuteronomy 27-29)! Evil within the
community must be eradicated.

verses.zh: 要凭两三个人的口作见证将那当死的人治死；不可凭一个人的口作见证将他治死。
verses.en: At the testimony of two or three witnesses the person must be executed. They cannot be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.

verses.zh: 见证人要先下手，然后众民也下手将他治死。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉。
verses.en: The witnesses[NOTE:1] must be first to begin the execution, and then all the people[NOTE:2] are to join in afterward. In this way you will purge the evil from among you.
notes: Heb “the hand of the witnesses.” This means the two or three witnesses are to throw the first stones (cf. NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT).
Heb “the hand of all the people.”
verses.commentary:
17:7 "The hand of the witness shall be first against him" The ones who witnessed against a person
were to throw the first stones (cf. Deut. 13:9; Lev. 24:14). Thus, if the witnesses were lying, then God would punish
them for shedding innocent blood (i.e. murder).

verses.zh: 「你城中若起了争讼的事，或因流血，或因争竞，或因殴打，是你难断的案件，你就当起来，往耶和华―你　神所选择的地方
verses.en: If a matter is too difficult for you to judge—bloodshed,[NOTE:1] legal claim,[NOTE:2] or assault[NOTE:3]—matters of controversy in your villages[NOTE:4]—you must leave there and go up to the place the Lord your God chooses.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “between blood and blood.”
Heb “between claim and claim.”
Heb “between blow and blow.”
Heb “gates.”

Several Greek recensions add “to place his name there,” thus completing the usual formula to describe the central sanctuary (cf. Deut 12:5, 11, 14, 18; 16:6). However, the context suggests that the local Levitical towns, and not the central sanctuary, are in mind.
verses.commentary:
17:8 The very difficult (BDB 810, KB 927, Niphal IMPERFECT) cases were to be referred
to the priests at the central sanctuary (cf. Deut. 12:5,11,13).

These types of judicial difficulties are described as:

- "blood to blood" (BDB 196), meaning

- a fight between two people

- a feud between two families

- murder or manslaughteer

- "judgment to judgment" (BDB 192)

- NRSV, "one kind of legal right and another"

- TEV, "certain cases of property rights"

- NJB, "conflicting claims"

- REB, "civil rights"

- JPSOA, "civil law"

- NET Bible, "legal claim"

- NIV, "lawsuits"

- "stroke to stroke" (BDB 619), meaning some kind of assault (cf. Deut. 21:5)

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 405, asserts that the difficult cases involved a lack of
evidence. By referring these to the priests at the central sanctuary, Moses is assuming that divine insight
will determine the guilt or innocence of the parties involved.

▣ "the place which the Lord your God chooses" This VERB
(BDB 103, KB 119) is used in Deuteronomy for several things:

- YHWH's choice of Israel's forefathers, Deut. 4:37

- YHWH's choice of Israel, Deut. 7:6,7; 10:15; 14:2

- YHWH's choice of the place of a central sanctuary, Deut. 12:5,11,14,18,21,26; 14:23,24,25; 15:20;
16:2,6,7,11,15,16; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2; 31:11

- YHWH's choice of a king, Deut. 17:15

- YHWH's choice of an Aaronic (Levitical) priesthood, Deut. 18:5; 21:5

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

verses.zh: 去见祭司利未人，并当时的审判官，求问他们，他们必将判语指示你。
verses.en: You will go to the Levitical priests and the judge in office in those days and seek a solution; they will render a verdict.
verses.commentary:
17:9 "the Levitical priest" The Masoretic Text (Hebrew), the Septuagint (Greek), and the Peshitta (Aramaic) have
the PLURAL, "priests." This indicates a pool or guild of priests (cf. Deut. 19:17). This was the rabbinical proof
text for the Sanhedrin (set up by Ezra).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANHEDRIN

(cf. 2 Chr. 19:11 for historical example of this) or leader of a group of judges.

verses.zh: 他们在耶和华所选择的地方指示你的判语，你必照着他们所指教你的一切话谨守遵行。
verses.en: You must then do as they have determined at that place the Lord chooses. Be careful to do just as you are taught.

verses.zh: 要按他们所指教你的律法，照他们所断定的去行；他们所指示你的判语，你不可偏离左右。
verses.en: You must do what you are instructed, and the verdict they pronounce to you, without fail. Do not deviate right or left from what they tell you.
verses.commentary:
17:11 "you shall not turn aside from the word. . .to the right or the left" This is a Hebrew idiom for not changing
the verdict and punishment handed down by the Levitical judges. Similar imagery is used of YHWH's words in
Deut. 4:2; 12:32. Once YHWH's will is known, turning right or left means disobedience (cf. Deut. 5:32; 17:20; 28:14;
Josh. 1:7; 23:6; 2 Kgs. 22:2; Prov. 4:27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 若有人擅敢不听从那侍立在耶和华―你　神面前的祭司，或不听从审判官，那人就必治死；这样，便将那恶从以色列中除掉。
verses.en: The person who pays no attention[NOTE:1] to the priest currently serving the Lord your God there, or to the judge—that person must die, so that you may purge evil from Israel.
notes: Heb “who acts presumptuously not to listen” (cf. NASB).
verses.commentary:
17:12 "presumptuously" This term (BDB 268) is used of wilful disobedience (cf. Deut. 1:43; 17:12,13; 18:20,22). The
judge and priest were representatives of YHWH's authority. Therefore, to reject their decisions was to reject YHWH! In
Deut. 18:20-22, it is prophets who do not know YHWH speaking in His name, using His authority!

SPECIAL TOPIC: UNINTENTIONAL SINS

▣ "the priest who stand there to serve the Lord" This is imagery for a Levitical priest
who served at the central sanctuary or tabernacle.

▣

"you shall purge the evil from Israel"

"You must banish this evil from Israel"

"you will sweep out evil from Israel"

"you shall remove the evil one from Israel"

The VERB (BDB 128, KB 145, Piel PERFECT with waw) means to

verses.zh: 众百姓都要听见害怕，不再擅敢行事。」
verses.en: Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and not be so presumptuous again.

verses.zh: 「到了耶和华―你　神所赐你的地，得了那地居住的时候，若说：『我要立王治理我，像四围的国一样。』
verses.en: When you come to the land the Lord your God is giving you and take it over and live in it and then say, “I will select a king like all the nations surrounding me,”
verses.commentary:
17:14-20 These are some of the most controversial verses in the OT, especially the Pentateuch. These
verses speak about a coming king. Many OT scholars of our day say that Deuteronomy is the book that was found
during Josiah's reform hundreds of years later during the monarchial period, and that it was written by the priests
at that time to centralize worship at Jerusalem (cf. 2 Kgs. 22:8; 2 Chr. 34:14-15). They assert that this is evidence that it
was not written by Moses because nowhere else in the Pentateuch is there mention of a king. It is an anachronism
referring to Solomon, so obviously it must have been written later. I do not believe any of this! Some verses which
show that Deut. 17:14-20 are not unique in the Pentateuch are Gen. 17:6, 35:11; 36:31;
Num. 24:7; Jdg. 8:22,23; 9:6. See Special Topics below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSAIC AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

It is interesting to note the differences between the kings of the ANE and Israel's future kings.

- ANE kings had full control but Israel's king is limited and must follow YHWH's will

- ANE kings gave the laws of the land but Israel's king received YHWH's Law

- ANE kings were the final civil authority but Israel's kings were not; it was the judges who were to deliver YHWH's verdicts

17:14 "and you say, 'I will set a king over me like all the nations who are around me'" The VERB is
a Qal COHORTATIVE (BDB 962, KB 1321). It is repeated four times in Deut. 17:14 and 15. The second
(Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE) and third (Qal IMPERFECT with waw)
usages go together as a way of intensification:

- NASB, NKJV "you shall surely set"

- NRSV "you may indeed set"

- TEV "be sure"

The problem was not a king, but the descriptive phrase, "a king like all the nations who are around me"! The king
was to represent YHWH (cf. Deut. 17:8), not ANE pagan courts. This very issue is dealt with when Israel
asked Samuel for a king in 1 Samuel 8.

verses.zh: 你总要立耶和华―你　神所拣选的人为王。必从你弟兄中立一人；不可立你弟兄以外的人为王。
verses.en: you must select without fail[NOTE:1] a king whom the Lord your God chooses. From among your fellow citizens[NOTE:2] you must appoint a king—you may not designate a foreigner who is not one of your fellow Israelites.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, indicated in the translation by the words “without fail.”
Heb “your brothers,” but not referring to siblings (cf. NIV11, NLT “fellow Israelite”). The same phrase also occurs in v. 20.
Heb “your brothers.” See the preceding note on “fellow citizens.”
verses.commentary:
17:15 "whom the Lord your God chooses" YHWH is sovereign, He (not Israel,
cf. Deut. 17:14) chooses the man, but Israel confirms His choice by their affirmation (e.g. Jdgs. 11:11; Hosea 1:11).

Notice the guidelines for kingship:

- when Israel possesses the land, Deut. 17:14

- one whom YHWH chooses, Deut. 17:15

- not a foreigner, Deut. 17:15

- he shall not trust in military armament ("multiply horses"), Deut. 17:16

- he shall not seek help from Egypt, Deut. 17:16

- he shall not trust in political allegiances ("multiply wives"), Deut. 17:17

- he shall not trust in wealth ("increase silver and gold"), Deut. 17:17

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

The numbers 4-7 above reflect Solomon's abuses! It is unique in Ancient Near Eastern law that
the king has his powers limited, but in Israel God:

- sets the place and procedures of justice

- sets the pattern of worship

- sets limits on kingly power, succession, and wealth

- the king is one among many covenant partners (cf. Deut. 17:20)

- the king must study regularly and implement (personally and officially) God's laws (cf. Deut. 17:18-19)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

verses.zh: 只是王不可为自己加添马匹，也不可使百姓回埃及去，为要加添他的马匹，因耶和华曾吩咐你们说：『不可再回那条路去。』
verses.en: Moreover, he must not accumulate horses for himself or allow the people to return to Egypt to do so,[NOTE:1] for the Lord has said you must never again return that way.
notes: Heb “in order to multiply horses.” The translation uses “do so” in place of “multiply horses” to avoid redundancy (cf. NAB, NIV).
verses.commentary:
17:16 "he shall not multiply horses" Horses were owned only by rulers, not local people. A horse was a battle
weapon for war. In other words, "Don't trust in your military might. I, YHWH, am protecting you."

▣ "You shall never again return that way" This possibly refers to a later practice of trading Hebrew
mercenaries for horses. One historical example is the Elephantine community. However, in context, it again asserts
that the coming king must trust totally in YHWH alone!

verses.zh: 他也不可为自己多立妃嫔，恐怕他的心偏邪；也不可为自己多积金银。
verses.en: Furthermore, he must not marry many[NOTE:1] wives lest his affections turn aside, and he must not accumulate much silver and gold.
notes: Heb “must not multiply” (cf. KJV, NASB); NLT “must not take many.”
verses.commentary:
17:17 "He shall not multiply wives" This refers to (1) lustful use of power or more probably (2) political and
religious alliances. This was the Ancient Near Eastern way to form "non-aggression" pacts.

▣ "also his heart will turn away" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "nor shall he greatly increase silver and gold for himself" YHWH placed the king as His under
shepherd. That under shepherd should never strive for personal wealth or power.

verses.zh: 他登了国位，就要将祭司利未人面前的这律法书，为自己抄录一本，
verses.en: When he sits on his royal throne he must make a copy of this law[NOTE:1] on a scroll[NOTE:2] given to him by the Levitical priests.
notes: Or “instruction.” The LXX reads here τὸ δευτερονόμιον τοῦτο (to deuteronomion touto, “this second law”). From this Greek phrase the present name of the book, “Deuteronomy” or “second law” (i.e., the second giving of the law), is derived. However, the MT’s expression מִשְׁנֶה הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת (mishneh hattorah hazzoʾt) is better rendered “copy of this law.” Here the term תּוֹרָה (torah) probably refers only to the book of Deuteronomy and not to the whole Pentateuch.

The Hebrew term סֵפֶר (sefer) means a “writing” or “document” and could be translated “book” (so KJV, ASV, TEV). However, since “book” carries the connotation of a modern bound book with pages (an obvious anachronism) it is preferable to render the Hebrew term “scroll” here and elsewhere.
verses.commentary:
17:18-20 These verses are a summary of the king's relationship to God's revealed will (i.e. the Law).

17:18 "he shall write for himself copy of this law" This probably refers to someone (i.e. a Levitical priest)
making a copy for him (cf. 2 Kgs. 11:12). This is the verse from which the Septuagint got the title for the book of
Deuteronomy (i.e. the Second Law), but in context this verse refers to a second copy of the Law, not a revised version of the Law.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (Suzerain) TREATIES

verses.zh: 存在他那里，要平生诵读，好学习敬畏耶和华―他的　神，谨守遵行这律法书上的一切言语和这些律例，
verses.en: It must be with him constantly, and he must read it as long as he lives, so that he may learn to revere the Lord his God and observe all the words of this law and these statutes and carry them out.
verses.commentary:
17:19 This verse and v. 20 have a series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS, which flow from
the king's reading (BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal PERFECT with waw) and learning (BDB 540, KB 531,
Qal IMPERFECT) from YHWH's revelation of His will through Moses (i.e. Pentateuch; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL):

- "to fear" (BDB 431, KB 432; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR)

- "to keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- "to do" (BDB 793, KB 889)

- "heart not be lifted up above his countrymen" (BDB 926, KB 1202, cf. Deut. 8:14)

- "not turn aside from the commandment" (BDB 693, KB 747)

This copy of YHWH's law is to remain with the king (this refers to the first VERB in Deut. 17:19,
BDB 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT). This reflects the parallel of the Hittite treaties, where two copies
of the covenant were made. One was put in the temple of the covenant partners' deity (here YHWH's tabernacle) and the
other remained with the vassel king (i.e. to be read regularly so as to be in compliance).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (Suzerain) TREATIES

▣ "this law and these statutes" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

verses.zh: 免得他向弟兄心高气傲，偏左偏右，离了这诫命。这样，他和他的子孙便可在以色列中，在国位上年长日久。」
verses.en: Then he will not exalt himself above his fellow citizens or turn from the commandments to the right or left, and he and his descendants will enjoy many years ruling over his kingdom[NOTE:1] in Israel.
notes: Heb “upon his kingship.” Smr supplies כִּסֵא (kiseʾ, “throne”) so as to read “upon the throne of his kingship.” This overliteralizes what is a clearly understood figure of speech.
verses.commentary:
17:20 "to the right or the left" This is a Hebrew idiom of obedience. YHWH's will was described as a "path"
or "trail." It was clearly marked (by the Law). Israelites (as well as their king) were to stay on the path (e.g. Ps. 119:105), which
referred to lifestyle (e.g. Prov. 6:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "so that he and his sons may continue long in his kingdom" Kingship, like the high priesthood, was
to be a hereditary descent. The kingship (i.e. later concept of Messiah) was predicted to be in the line of Judah
(cf. Gen. 49:10) and the family of Jesse (cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES OF THE SPECIAL COMING ONE
